pairs.why: A's drum shells and stage have soft, moderate sheen like the real kit, while B adds hot specular streaks on the shells, hardware and stage rim that look lacquered.

A's posts and planks are smoother with less grain, while B's big post grain and sharper rope detail are more decorative than the real cards' smooth painted wood; both water surfaces are caustic-heavy.
Both have a satin dark body with soft highlights and a glossier metal truss, and neither differs from the real card enough on surface finish to prefer one.
Both have smooth, moderately glossy plastic with similar small-button detail and highlights, so surface finish gives no reason to choose.
A's leaves are smaller and softer with a calmer sheen, closer to the real matte clustered foliage, while B's larger leaves have crisp yellow specular edges.
Both match the real smooth matte rubber with glossy straps and evenly sized bump dots, with no meaningful difference in finish.
A's sand is smoother with soft ripples and its ball has soft highlights, while B's sand is a fine noisy grain, which is the texture-y direction the lessons reject.
B's gloves are slightly smoother with softer creases, closer to the real gloves' smooth leather, while A shows more wrinkles and crisp seams.
